posted.title: Primary outcome: defined before, not after

points.heading: What the item asks
points.body: Define every pre-specified primary and secondary outcome: the measure, how it was assessed, and exactly when.

points.heading: Why it matters
points.body: Vague outcomes invite switching after the data are in, one of the best-documented sources of reporting bias.

points.heading: How to comply
points.body: Write each outcome as: instrument + metric + aggregation + time point. Example: pain on a 0–10 scale, mean change at 12 weeks.

posted.takeaway: An outcome is pre-specified only if measure, metric and time point are written down first.

GG-PAR-25-145.title: Clinical Characterization of Cancer Therapy-induced Adverse Sequelae and Mechanism-based Interventional Strategies
GG-PAR-25-145.programme_family: NIH – US National Institutes of Health
GG-PAR-25-145.summary: This funding opportunity supports basic, translational, and clinical research to address chronic or delayed adverse effects of cancer therapies. The goal is to identify biological mechanisms, characterize clinical phenotypes, and develop interventional strategies to prevent or minimize long-term sequelae. Projects may include mechanistic studies, longitudinal phenotyping, and validation of clinical endpoints like biomarkers or patient-reported outcomes. Eligible applicants include higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit organizations, and foreign entities.

GG-PAR-25-265.programme: Hunter Kelly Newborn Screening Research Program
GG-PAR-25-265.programme_family: NIH – US National Institutes of Health
GG-PAR-25-265.summary: This funding opportunity supports research to develop novel screening approaches and therapeutic interventions for conditions currently in newborn screening panels or fatal/disabling genetic conditions that could benefit from early detection. Higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit businesses, and non-domestic (foreign) organizations are eligible to apply as lead entities.

GG-PAR-25-227.title: Natural History of Disorders Screenable in the Newborn Period (R01 Clinical Trial Optional)
GG-PAR-25-227.programme_family: NIH – US National Institutes of Health
GG-PAR-25-227.summary: This funding opportunity encourages applications to expand knowledge of the natural history of disorders that currently are, or may become, part of newborn screening programs. Funded R01 research project grants (clinical trial optional) aim to improve diagnostic accuracy, characterize disease progression, and support targeted therapeutic interventions. Higher education institutions, non-profits, for-profit businesses, government entities, and foreign (non-U.S.) organizations are eligible to apply as lead applicants.
